Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy evaluation

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative fluorescent multiplex PCR assay for PMP22 gene duplication/deletion

METHODOLOGY
Quantitative fluorescent multiplex PCR analysis was performed to detect copy number variations in the PMP22 gene (peripheral myelin protein 22). This assay detects the common 1.4 Mb duplication and deletion on chromosome 17p11.2 associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A) and hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies (HNPP), respectively. The test error rate is <1%.

RESULTS
PMP22 gene copy number: Normal (2 copies)
No PMP22 gene duplication or deletion detected

INTERPRETATION
This patient does not carry the common 1.4 Mb duplication of chromosome 17p11.2 containing the PMP22 gene that accounts for approximately 70% of CMT1A cases. The absence of this duplication does not exclude a diagnosis of CMT1A or other forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

RECOMMENDATIONS
If clinical findings continue to support a diagnosis of CMT1 (demyelinating form), consider:
1. Point mutation screening in the PMP22 gene
2. Sequence analysis of the P0 (MPZ) gene
3. Comprehensive CMT gene panel testing if indicated

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.
